name: Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia

criteria.description: Subacute onset of respiratory symptoms including cough and dyspnea lasting weeks to months
Chest imaging showing patchy bilateral alveolar opacities, often peripheral or peribronchial
Lung biopsy demonstrating intra-alveolar granulation tissue plugs (Masson bodies) with preservation of lung architecture
Exclusion of secondary causes such as infections, connective tissue diseases, or drug-induced lung injury
Restrictive ventilatory defect and reduced diffusing capacity on pulmonary function testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms, characteristic radiographic findings, histopathologic confirmation, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary discussion including pulmonology, radiology, and pathology

imaging: Chest X-ray showing patchy bilateral alveolar infiltrates
High-resolution CT demonstrating peripheral and peribronchial consolidation with ground-glass opacities
Absence of honeycombing or significant fibrosis
other: Histopathology showing intra-alveolar buds of granulation tissue (Masson bodies)
Pulmonary function tests indicating restrictive defect and decreased diffusing capacity

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive fibrosis with honeycombing on imaging
Histopathology showing usual interstitial pneumonia pattern
Acute onset with systemic signs of infection
Imaging showing centrilobular nodules and air trapping

redFlags: Failure to respond to corticosteroid therapy
references: Cordier JF. Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. Eur Respir J. 2006;28(2):422-46.
King TE Jr, et al. Idiopathic interstitial pneumonias: diagnosis and treatment. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2001;164(6):1023-42.

American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002;165(2):277-304.
